title: Jadumani Singh Batters Scottish Favourite to Storm Into CWG 2026 Boxing Pre-Quarters
excerpt: The 22-year-old from Manipur dominated every round against home crowd favourite Aaron Cullen, earning a 5-0 unanimous decision in his Commonwealth Games debut at Glasgow.
body:
• Indian boxer Jadumani Singh Mandengbam won his men's 55 kg opening bout by a 5-0 unanimous decision against Scotland's Aaron Cullen at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games.
  • The 22-year-old Manipuri dominated all three rounds, earning straight 10s on every scorecard against Cullen's 9s.
  • Jadumani will next face Pakistan's Sumama Rehman in the pre-quarterfinals.
  • Olympic bronze medallist Lovlina Borgohain has already guaranteed at least a bronze in the women's 75 kg category due to a small five-entry field.

A Clinical Opening Statement

Indian boxer Jadumani Singh Mandengbam announced his arrival at the 2026 Commonwealth Games with a thoroughly one-sided victory over Scotland's Aaron Cullen in the men's 55 kg opening round on Friday. The 22-year-old from Manipur won by a 5-0 unanimous decision, dominating all three rounds against the home crowd favourite at Glasgow's Emirates Arena.

"The 22-year-old from Manipur won by a 5-0 unanimous decision, dominating all three rounds against the home crowd favourite at Glasgow's Emirates Arena."

Jadumani built an insurmountable lead by controlling the first two rounds with sharp combinations and superior ring movement. In the third, he shifted to a firm defensive posture, conserving energy while maintaining distance. The judges' scorecards reflected his complete authority: straight 10s across every round against Cullen's straight 9s.

From Patiala Trials to Glasgow Ring

Jadumani earned his spot on the CWG squad after winning the national selection trials in Patiala earlier this year. He followed that up with a silver medal at the World Boxing Cup Finals, establishing himself as one of Indian boxing's brightest prospects at bantamweight.

His selection was not without drama. The sports ministry initially sought clarification from the Boxing Federation of India over his inclusion in the squad, delaying confirmation before ultimately clearing him to travel with the team.

Next: Pakistan's Sumama Rehman

Jadumani's pre-quarterfinal bout against Pakistan's Sumama Rehman adds a layer of rivalry to an already electric Glasgow atmosphere. A win would put the Manipuri boxer in the quarterfinals, within two victories of a guaranteed medal.

India's Boxing Campaign So Far

India has sent a strong seven-man, seven-woman boxing contingent to Glasgow. Olympic bronze medallist Lovlina Borgohain has already secured at least a bronze medal in the women's 75 kg category — with only five entries in the division, she received a direct passage to the semifinals without throwing a punch.

The boxing program is one of India's strongest medal prospects at this Games, alongside para powerlifting, where Jhandu Kumar won India's first medal of the CWG on Day 1, and athletics, where Neeraj Chopra leads the contingent.
